Subject: EnterpriseCorp — post-discovery: stakeholders & procurement path

Thanks again for the time today — great discussion. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

Summary of the call:
- Use case: embed Redwood inference into EnterpriseCorp search/productivity flows (internal + customer-facing).
- Key decision criteria: latency under 200ms p50, data residency controls, audit logs, and predictable unit economics.

Stakeholder map (from the call):
- Economic buyer: Samir Patel (VP Product)
- Security/compliance: Katie Reynolds (Head of Security)
- Procurement/legal: procurement@enterprisecorp.com (TBD contact)
- Day-to-day owner: Lina Gomez (PM; not on today's call)

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Katie — can you share the procurement contact and any standard timelines for SOW/PO processing?
2) We’ll send an initial SOW + draft quote and the completed Redwood security questionnaire.
3) We understand you may want non-standard payment terms (60 days) and a custom SLA — please confirm details so we can route for internal review.

Attachments: Redwood_Draft_SOW_v1.docx (draft scope)

Happy to hop on another call with procurement/legal if helpful.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Subject: Fwd: EnterpriseCorp — procurement asks & security questionnaire — request for approval (discount + payment + SLA)

Aditya / Dylan — forwarding the procurement asks from EnterpriseCorp. Summary of ask from the customer: 

- Net 60 payment terms (EnterpriseCorp requires Net 60)
- SLA: 99.9% uptime for customer-facing endpoints with financial credits on breach
- Compliance: SOC 2 Type II report and DPA required prior to PO
- Timeline: need an updated SOW/quote by 2027-03-11

My recommended commercial approach to keep momentum:
- Offer a first-year 15% onboarding discount off list for the initially scoped committed capacity (to align incentives).
- Approve Net 60 for EnterpriseCorp given the size & strategic fit, but require a PO as commit and add a clause for late-payment interest.
- For SLA, propose to accept 99.9% target but add capped credit schedule and require DPA/SOC2 attestation before SLA goes into effect.

Attachments: Redwood_Draft_SOW_v1.docx (redlines to follow after legal review)

Can you confirm internal approval for: 15% discount + Net 60 + conditional SLA as described? If approved I'll update the SOW/quote and send completed security questionnaire.

Thanks — Marissa

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: 2027-03-05T17:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: EnterpriseCorp — procurement asks & security questionnaire — request for approval (discount + payment + SLA)

On Fri, Mar 5, 2027 at 1:02 PM Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com> wrote:
> Aditya / Dylan — forwarding the procurement asks from EnterpriseCorp. Summary of ask from the customer: 
> 
> - Net 60 payment terms (EnterpriseCorp requires Net 60)
> - SLA: 99.9% uptime for customer-facing endpoints with financial credits on breach
> - Compliance: SOC 2 Type II report and DPA required prior to PO
> 
Thanks for the summary. Legal view / recommended guardrails:

1) Payment terms: Net 60 is acceptable for this counterparty provided we have an executed PO and an approved credit check in our CRM. We should add language for interest/late fee at X% if payment extends beyond N days (finance to confirm).

2) Discount: Approve a max of 15% first-year discount. Any deeper concession requires SVP/Revenue approval. Tie the discount to an annual committed commitment size in SOW.

3) SLA: We can agree to 99.9% availability for hosted endpoints but recommend: 
   - SLA becomes effective after verification of SOC2 attestation and DPA execution.
   - Credits capped at 3 months' recurring fees per rolling 12-month window.
   - Exclude downtime caused by customer misconfiguration or force majeure.

4) Compliance: We will provide SOC 2 Type II report and DPA. However, if the customer requires SOC 2 on-prem verification or additional controls, that could trigger a security exception review and additional costs.

If Finance gives the green light on Net 60 (credit check + invoice process), we can move forward with Marissa's recommended commercial approach (15% discount + Net 60 + conditional SLA).

\u0014Dylan
Legal Counsel | Redwood Inference
dylan_brooks@redwood.com

- Net 60 payment terms, contingent on receipt of an executed PO and a successful credit check by Finance.
